parsed.rationale: Leads II, III and aVF show ST elevation with broad, hyperacute-looking T waves, and reciprocal ST depression with T inversion in aVL and lead I, which fits an acute inferior STEMI. Concave elevation is also seen in the lateral leads (V4–V6), so pericarditis is a differential. This is a visual read only, and the elevation in lead III is only about 1 mm.
